profit and contribution formulas / The LTGP:CAC ratio: calculating Lifetime Gross Profit (after COGS and delivery costs) against Customer Acquisition Cost (Ad Spend / New Customers). The necessity of placing a time constraint (e.g., 30-day, 90-day, 365-day) on LTGP based on the brand's repeat purchase frequency. Splitting the P&L: generating a "first-time customer P&L" vs. a "returning customer P&L" to identify if returning revenue is masking unprofitable acquisition.

The benchmarks for LTGP:CAC ratios: <1 is a death spiral (losing money on first purchase without exceptional retention), 1-2 requires extremely lean operating expenses, 2-3 is the target scale zone, and >3 means underinvesting in acquisition. The formula for CAC: Total Ad Spend / New Customers Acquired. The definition of LTGP: Gross Profit generated over a constrained time period, minus COGS and cost of delivery. The specific retention benchmarks for different verticals by day 365: 55% lift for fashion, 110% lift for CPG/supplements, and near 0% for furniture/homewares (where only day-0 GP matters). The relationship between CPC, CTR, CPM, and CAC: CAC = (CTR x CPM) / Conversion Rate.

Broad agency pitches, hiring links, or general commentary on the macroeconomic environment (e.g., interest rates, iOS 14). Vague complaints about agencies defaulting to "creative problems" instead of structural problems.
